_doc: Asiddha domains — where the effect of one rule is invisible to another. Sūtra texts come from sutra_ref_out/ (ashtadhyayi corpus); the ranges are structural and each one says below what authorises it.

tripadi.range_authority: The tripāḍī is the standard closing section 8.2.1–8.4.68; the same bounds already govern engine/gates.py and engine/phase.py.
tripadi.reading: पूर्वत्र असिद्धम् — what a tripāḍī rule does is asiddha for everything earlier, including earlier tripāḍī rules.

abhiya.range_authority: आ भात् — up to भस्य (6.4.129), which this engine already registers as the ADHIKARA that opens the bha section.
abhiya.reading: असिद्धवत् अत्र आ भात् — inside this section the rules are asiddhavat to one another.

ekadesha_for_satva_tuk.range_authority: The ekādeśa section opened by एकः पूर्वपरयोः (6.1.84). The observer sets are the ṣatva and tuk rules THIS ENGINE models, not an exhaustive reading of the śāstra.
ekadesha_for_satva_tuk.reading: षत्व-तुकोः असिद्धः — the ekādeśa is asiddha for ṣatva and for tuk.

tripadi_nimitta_exceptions.authority: Kāśikā 6.3.111 (ashtadhyayi.com row 63111) — ढ्रलोपे names the lopa of 8.3.13 ढो ढे लोपः / 8.3.14 रो रि as its own nimitta; were that lopa asiddha the rule would have no scope (vacana-sāmarthya). Udāharaṇa लीढम्, मीढम्, उपगूढम्; 6.3.112 सोढा, वोढा.
tripadi_nimitta_exceptions.reading: ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः — the dīrgha / ओत् sees the tripāḍī lopa that is its condition, and runs inside the tripāḍī right after it.

not_modelled: 6.1.86's observer sets are those the engine implements; more ṣatva/tuk rules will need adding as they land.
Asiddhatva inside the ābhīya section is modelled as full mutual invisibility; the tradition's exceptions (e.g. for a rule's own nimitta) are not yet distinguished.
